verifications.note: Jiangxi Provincial Investment Group bond tracking report (35pp), states the operating subsidiary 江西省天然气管道有限公司 is 54%-held by 江西省天然气集团 and 46%-held by the PipeChina subsidiary; names only the SYSTEM (省天然气管网一期/二期), not this trunk.

2022 CCXI credit rating report for 江西省天然气集团有限公司 (25pp), footnote states the identical 54% stake in 天然气管道公司, the entity 'responsible for investing/building/operating' the ENTIRE Phase I network (which includes this segment). Independent publisher class (rating agency vs. exchange bond disclosure).
2026 CCXI credit rating report, same publisher as above one year later, reconfirms the 54.00% stake in tabular form; also states 长输管网长度达3,182公里 system-wide as of 2026-03.

fills.researcher_notes:
Owner was blank. No source names this trunk's ownership individually -- Phase I is one integrated network built/owned under one corporate structure, so a system-level source is the right evidence for THIS cell (the brief's stated exception): the 54%/46% ownership split of the operating subsidiary (天然气管道公司) is a corporate/legal fact uniform across every segment of the network, unlike a physical fact such as length or diameter that varies segment-by-segment. Two independent document classes agree on the exact 54%/46% split (SSE bond disclosure vs. CCXI credit-rating reports, the latter corroborated across two vintages a year apart), so independent=true; keeping tier at medium rather than high because none of the three names this specific trunk. Matches the wiki's existing (uncited) Owner note for this row almost verbatim, which is a useful cross-check but was NOT used as a source per standing rule 1. 2022 CCXI report independently states 天然气管道公司 built/operates the 一期管网 that 承接川气东送气源 -- corroborates the same fuel-source fact for the whole Phase I network from a different publisher class (rating agency vs. government plan), though at system level only.

The qianzhan DRC plan names 九江-沙河 explicitly in the same sentence that establishes the Phase I network is fed by 川气东送 (Sichuan-East Gas Transmission Project) gas -- a genuine segment-level naming for this fact, not an aggregate-vs-segment violation. The CCXI 2022 report corroborates the same underlying fact for the network as a whole (different publisher, same conclusion). Keeping tier at medium rather than high since only one of the two sources names the segment directly; flagging for optional upgrade to high if the orchestrator judges the CCXI corroboration sufficient given the exception logic used for Owner above.
